extraction.name: SCIENCE QA
extraction.description: A large-scale multimodal multiple-choice science question answering benchmark with 21,208 examples, including questions, multiple-choice options, multimodal contexts, and annotations of answers with grounded lectures and explanations.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.publisher: Allen Institute for AI; University of California, Los Angeles; Arizona State University
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Mishra, S., Xia, T., Qiu, L., Chang, K.-W., Zhu, S.-C., Tafjord, O., Clark, P., & Kalyan, A. (2022). Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in the SCIENCE QA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in K-12 education. The authors downloaded the original science problems, extracted components such as questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions using heuristic rules, manually removed invalid or duplicated questions, shuffled answer options, and used semi-automated scripts to reformat lectures and solutions. Incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Not explicitly discussed as missing data; however, the paper reports that some questions have text context, image context, both, or no context, and that most questions are annotated with lectures and explanations rather than all questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open resources managed by IXL Learning; science problems aligned with California Common Core Content Standards.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Answer options were shuffled to avoid any specific pattern. Lectures and solutions were reformatted using semi-automated scripts so that special structures such as tables and lists are distinguishable from plain text.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid questions were manually removed, including questions with only one choice, faulty data, and duplicates. If multiple correct answers applied, only one correct answer was kept.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions were annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations. The paper states that incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts. For human evaluation of generated explanations, AMT workers rated relevance, correctness, and completeness, and majority vote determined the final human scores.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For generated explanations, annotators rated explanations as relevant, correct, and complete; final scores were determined by majority vote. The paper also reports that 65.2% of GPT-3 (CoT) explanations met the gold standard of human evaluations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Most questions have one lecture and one explanation; for human evaluation of generated explanations, each batch was assigned to 3 workers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For the human performance study, only workers who obtained a high school or higher degree and passed qualification examples were qualified.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 was used to extract image captions; the paper also mentions using the tool2 captioning model for images in experimental details.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code are available at https://scienceqa.github.io. The paper states the dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes only, but does not specify a versioning or update schedule.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper states that the dataset does not contain personally identifiable information or personally sensitive information such as gender and race.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is proposed to diagnose multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems and may support K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. The authors state that the work aims at AI for the common good and that antisocial data points will be removed based on feedback.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper does not explicitly describe dataset bias, but notes that the dataset spans diverse subjects, topics, categories, skills, grades, and context types to increase diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that image captions lack fine-grained semantics and usually do not work well for diagrams, which can cause failures. It also reports that models may fail on complex or uncommon domain knowledge and that some generated explanations can be irrelevant, incorrect, or incomplete.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal question answering, multi-hop reasoning, and chain-of-thought reasoning; training, validation, and testing splits are provided. The paper also discusses fine-tuning and few-shot prompting use cases for UnifiedQA and GPT-3.
